# Endpoint Protection & Device Controls Procedure

## Purpose

This procedure provides the operational instructions Endpoint Engineering follows to deploy, configure, and continuously verify malicious code protection, spam protection, memory protection, mobile code controls, and device/media restrictions across Example Org systems. Executing it produces the evidence artifacts — the EDR deployment coverage report and the removable media policy configuration — required to demonstrate conformance to the Endpoint Protection & Device Controls Standard.

## Scope

This procedure is performed by Endpoint Engineering on all organization-owned endpoints (workstations, notebook computers, mobile devices) and on system entry and exit points including firewalls, remote-access servers, email servers, web servers, and proxy servers. It applies continuously, from initial deployment through ongoing configuration, testing, and response activities.

## Prerequisites

- Administrative access to the organization's [Endpoint Protection Platform] management console.
- Administrative access to the organization's [Email Security Gateway].
- Administrative access to the organization's [Endpoint Configuration Management Tool] for policy push and enforcement.
- Access to the [Ticketing System] for change requests, exception tracking, and incident handoffs.
- Access to the [Identity Provider] to confirm privileged-role membership for update and verification actions.
- A current copy of the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan (SSPP) for documenting alternative actions and mobile code definitions.
- Approval from Endpoint Engineering for any policy change executed under this procedure.

## Procedure Steps

### Deploy Malicious Code Protection at Entry and Exit Points [NIST SI-3 (Low, Moderate, High)]

1. Endpoint Engineering identifies all system entry and exit points in scope — firewalls, remote-access servers, workstations, email servers, web servers, proxy servers, notebook computers, and mobile devices — using the [Endpoint Configuration Management Tool] inventory.
1. Install the malicious code protection agent from the [Endpoint Protection Platform] on every identified system, pushing via the [Endpoint Configuration Management Tool].
1. Verify agent installation and health on each system from the [Endpoint Protection Platform] console.
1. Generate the EDR deployment coverage report from the [Endpoint Protection Platform] and reconcile it against the inventory; investigate and remediate any gap on a system that reports no agent.
1. Retain the EDR deployment coverage report as evidence of implementation.

### Enable Both Signature-Based and Non-Signature-Based Detection [ARC-AMPE SI-3 (AE Mandatory)]

1. In the [Endpoint Protection Platform], enable the signature-based detection engine on all managed endpoints and entry/exit point systems.
1. Enable the non-signature-based detection engine (behavioral/heuristic analysis) alongside the signature engine on the same systems.
1. Confirm both engines show as active — not disabled or in passive mode — for every system in the deployment coverage report.

### Update Malicious Code Protection Mechanisms [NIST SI-3 (Low, Moderate, High) | ARC-AMPE SI-3 (AE Mandatory) | NIST SI-3(4)]

1. In the [Endpoint Protection Platform], enable automatic signature and engine updates so that protection mechanisms update as new releases become available, in accordance with organizational configuration management policies and procedures.
1. Restrict the ability to approve or manually trigger protection mechanism updates to users holding the privileged role in the [Identity Provider]; updates occur only when directed by such a privileged user.
1. Route any request for a non-standard update (delayed rollback, deferred deployment) through the [Ticketing System] as a change request reviewed and approved by Endpoint Engineering.

### Configure Periodic Scans [NIST SI-3 (Low, Moderate, High) | ARC-AMPE SI-3 (AE Mandatory)]

1. In the [Endpoint Protection Platform], set the scheduled scan policy for all managed systems to run at a minimum of every one (1) week.
1. Apply the scan schedule consistently across the full endpoint fleet via the [Endpoint Configuration Management Tool].
1. Review scan completion status in the [Endpoint Protection Platform] console and follow up on systems that miss their scheduled scan.

### Configure Real-Time Scanning of Files from External Sources [NIST SI-3 (Low, Moderate, High) | ARC-AMPE SI-3 (AE Mandatory)]

1. In the [Endpoint Protection Platform], enable real-time, on-access scanning of files downloaded, opened, or executed from external sources on all endpoints.
1. On the network entry and exit points (firewalls, email servers, web servers, proxy servers, remote-access servers), enable equivalent real-time file scanning at the [Email Security Gateway] and [Endpoint Protection Platform] network components.
1. Verify both endpoint-level and network-level real-time scanning are active for each system in the EDR deployment coverage report, satisfying the requirement that external-source files are scanned at both locations.

### Configure Block, Quarantine, and Alerting on Detection [NIST SI-3 (Low, Moderate, High) | ARC-AMPE SI-3 (AE Mandatory)]

1. In the [Endpoint Protection Platform], set the detection response policy to **both** block and quarantine detected malicious code.
1. Configure the alerting policy to send a near real-time alert on every malicious code detection to the administrator and organization-defined security personnel — at minimum, [Security Operations].
1. Test the alert path by validating that a detection event generates the alert in the [Security Operations] alert queue.
1. Any action other than block-and-quarantine for a specific detection requires Endpoint Engineering approval, recorded in the [Ticketing System].

### Address False Positives [NIST SI-3 (Low, Moderate, High) | ARC-AMPE SI-3 (AE Mandatory)]

1. When a false positive is reported or observed, [Security Operations] or the system owner opens a ticket in the [Ticketing System] identifying the affected file, system, and detection rule.
1. Endpoint Engineering assesses the potential availability impact on the affected system and, if necessary, applies a narrowly scoped exclusion or rule exception in the [Endpoint Protection Platform].
1. Record the false positive, its analysis, and the remediation decision in the [Ticketing System]; review exclusions periodically to confirm each remains necessary.
1. Submit confirmed false positives to the protection vendor through its designated submission channel.

### Test Malicious Code Protection Mechanisms [NIST SI-3(6)]

1. At the [Testing Frequency], Endpoint Engineering introduces a known benign test file (e.g., an industry-standard test signature) into a managed system.
1. Verify that the [Endpoint Protection Platform] detects the test file, blocks or quarantines it per policy, and generates the associated alert to [Security Operations].
1. Confirm the detection produced the expected incident reporting in the alert queue; if detection or alerting fails, open a ticket in the [Ticketing System] and remediate before the next test cycle.
1. Record the test outcome as evidence of mechanism verification.

### Detect Unauthorized Operating System Commands via the Kernel API [NIST SI-3(8)]

1. In the [Endpoint Protection Platform], enable kernel-level behavioral monitoring on the organization-defined system hardware components.
1. Configure the policy to detect the organization-defined unauthorized operating system commands through the kernel API.
1. Set the response action to issue a warning, audit the command execution, and/or prevent execution of the command, per the organization-defined response for each command class.
1. Verify detections and audit records are flowing to the [Security Operations] alert queue.

### Analyze Malicious Code Characteristics and Behavior [NIST SI-3(10)]

1. When malicious code is detected that warrants deeper analysis, Endpoint Engineering employs the organization-defined analysis tools and techniques — including sandbox detonation and behavioral analysis in the [Endpoint Protection Platform] — to characterize the code.
1. Incorporate the analysis results into the organizational incident response process by attaching findings to the incident record in the [Incident Response Platform].
1. Incorporate the analysis results into the flaw remediation process by opening or updating the corresponding remediation item in the [Ticketing System], including any indicated patch or configuration change.

### Verify the Correct Operation of Security and Privacy Functions [NIST SI-6 (High) | ARC-AMPE SI-6 (AE Mandatory)]

1. In the [Endpoint Protection Platform], enable the self-verification capability so that security and privacy functions (e.g., agent integrity, policy enforcement, scanning engine health) are checked automatically upon system startup and/or restart.
1. Perform verification upon command by a user with appropriate privileges (via the [Identity Provider] privileged role) whenever a manual check is needed, and on a scheduled basis at least monthly.
1. Confirm that scheduled and startup verifications run on all in-scope systems and that results are captured by the platform.

### Alert on Failed Security and Privacy Verification Tests [NIST SI-6 (High) | ARC-AMPE SI-6 (AE Mandatory)]

1. Configure the [Endpoint Protection Platform] to send an alert to organization-defined personnel or roles — at a minimum, the system/security administrator — whenever a security or privacy verification test fails.
1. Validate the alert path to the administrator and [Security Operations] queues.

### Take Corrective Action on Verification Anomalies [NIST SI-6 (High) | ARC-AMPE SI-6 (AE Mandatory)]

1. When verification reveals anomalies, shut the system down, restart the system, or perform the organization-defined alternative action, as directed by Endpoint Engineering.
1. Under ARC-AMPE, if an alternative action (other than shutdown or restart) is selected, document that action in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan (SSPP) before relying on it.
1. Record the anomaly, the action taken, and the disposition in the [Ticketing System].

### Support Distributed Security Function Testing [NIST SI-6(2)]

1. Employ the automated mechanisms in the [Endpoint Protection Platform] and [Endpoint Configuration Management Tool] to orchestrate and manage security and privacy function testing across the distributed fleet, rather than per-system manual testing.
1. Use the central consoles to schedule tests, collect results, and track systems whose tests have not run.

### Report Security and Privacy Function Verification Results [NIST SI-6(3)]

1. Report the results of security and privacy function verification to organization-defined personnel or roles — at minimum, the system/security administrator and Endpoint Engineering leadership.
1. Deliver results through the reporting capability of the [Endpoint Protection Platform] and record delivery in the [Ticketing System].

### Implement and Maintain Spam Protection [NIST SI-8 (Moderate, High) | FedRAMP SI-8 | ARC-AMPE SI-8 (AE Mandatory) | NIST SI-8(2) | ARC-AMPE SI-8(2) | NIST SI-8(3)]

1. Endpoint Engineering implements spam protection mechanisms at the system entry and exit points — firewalls, remote-access servers, email servers, web servers, proxy servers, workstations, notebook computers, and mobile devices — using the [Email Security Gateway] and the endpoint protection policy in the [Endpoint Protection Platform].
1. Configure the mechanisms to detect and act on unsolicited messages (quarantine, tag, or reject per the gateway policy).
1. Enable automatic updates of the spam protection mechanisms — filter rules and reputation feeds — as new releases are available, in accordance with organizational configuration management policies and procedures, at an automatic update frequency of at least every one (1) week.
1. Enable the learning capability of the spam protection mechanisms (e.g., Bayesian/adaptive filtering and user feedback) so the mechanisms more effectively identify legitimate communications traffic over time.
1. Verify in the [Email Security Gateway] console that update jobs complete successfully and that learning features are active.

### Implement and Verify DMARC for Government-Sent Email [FedRAMP SI-8]

1. Where Example Org sends email on behalf of the government as part of the business offering, implement Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting & Conformance (DMARC) on the sending domain for outgoing messages as described in DHS Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 18-01.
1. Confirm the DMARC DNS configuration for each sending domain: the policy is set to `p=reject` and the `rua` parameter includes `reports@dmarc.cyber.dhs.gov`.
1. Document DMARC compliance in the SI-08 control implementation solution description.
1. List the FROM: domain(s) used when emails are sent on behalf of the government in the same control implementation documentation.

### Protect System Memory from Unauthorized Code Execution [NIST SI-16 (Moderate, High) | ARC-AMPE SI-16 (AE Mandatory)]

1. In the [Endpoint Protection Platform] and via the [Endpoint Configuration Management Tool], enable exploit mitigation controls on all in-scope systems, including at a minimum data execution prevention (DEP) and address space layout randomization (ASLR).
1. Apply the organization-defined additional memory protection controls defined for this control set where supported by the platform.
1. Verify the settings are applied and not overridable by standard users, and record the applied configuration as evidence.

### Restrict and Prohibit System Media Types [NIST MP-7 (Low, Moderate, High) | ARC-AMPE MP-7 (AE Mandatory) | NIST MP-7(2)]

1. Endpoint Engineering defines the organization-defined prohibited media types and systems in the device control policy within the [Endpoint Protection Platform].
1. Configure the device control policy to restrict or prohibit the use of those media types on the organization-defined systems and system components, and retain the resulting removable media policy configuration as evidence.
1. Prohibit the use of personally owned media — flash drives, external hard disk drives, and other portable storage and media devices — on organization-defined systems and networks, enforced by the same device control safeguards.
1. Prohibit the use of portable storage devices that have no identifiable owner on organizational systems.
1. Prohibit the use of sanitization-resistant media in organizational systems under the device control policy.
1. Route any request for a media-use exception through the [Ticketing System]; Endpoint Engineering reviews and approves or denies each exception and records the decision.

### Define and Control Mobile Code [NIST SC-18 (Moderate, High) | ARC-AMPE SC-18 (AE Mandatory) | ARC-AMPE SC-18 SSPP]

1. Endpoint Engineering defines the acceptable and unacceptable mobile code and mobile code technologies for the system (e.g., permitted scripting environments, prohibited plugin technologies).
1. Under ARC-AMPE, document the acceptable and unacceptable mobile code definitions in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan (SSPP).
1. Authorize, monitor, and control the use of acceptable mobile code within the system through browser/application policy and the [Endpoint Protection Platform].

### Detect and Act on Unacceptable Mobile Code [NIST SC-18(1)]

1. Configure the [Endpoint Protection Platform] to identify the organization-defined unacceptable mobile code types on managed systems and at entry/exit points.
1. Configure the organization-defined corrective actions — block, alert [Security Operations], and open a ticket in the [Ticketing System] — to execute automatically upon detection.

### Verify Mobile Code Before Deployment [NIST SC-18(2)]

1. Before any mobile code is acquired, developed, or deployed into the system, Endpoint Engineering verifies that it meets the organization-defined mobile code requirements established in the SSPP.
1. Record the verification and approval in the [Ticketing System] prior to deployment.

### Prevent Download and Execution of Unacceptable Mobile Code [NIST SC-18(3) | NIST SC-18(4)]

1. Configure web filtering and the [Endpoint Protection Platform] to prevent the download of the organization-defined unacceptable mobile code at network entry and exit points and on endpoints.
1. Configure the organization-defined software applications to prevent the automatic execution of mobile code, and enforce the organization-defined actions (e.g., user prompt, administrator approval) prior to any execution of mobile code.
1. Verify enforcement by attempting to load a known-blocked mobile code sample in a controlled test and confirming it is prevented.

### Confine Permitted Mobile Code Execution [NIST SC-18(5)]

1. Configure the environment so that permitted mobile code executes only within confined virtual machine environments.
1. Verify that no permitted mobile code executes outside the confined environment and that confinement settings cannot be modified by standard users.

## Roles & Responsibilities

Endpoint Engineering is accountable for this procedure end to end: it deploys, configures, tests, and reports on all malicious code protection, spam protection, memory protection, mobile code, and device control mechanisms, and it owns the handoffs to [Security Operations] and the [Incident Response Platform]. [Security Operations] and system/security administrators act on alerts and participate in testing and verification, and Endpoint Engineering reviews and approves all exceptions — false positive exclusions, media-use exceptions, alternative anomaly actions, and mobile code authorizations.

## Related Standard

This procedure operationalizes the **Endpoint Protection & Device Controls Standard**, which contains the full requirement text, the rationale for each control, and the framework mappings ([NIST], [FedRAMP], [ARC-AMPE]) referenced above.
